This Appeal Coming On For Hearing, Through
Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 06.11.2019 passed in MVC No.1905/2019 by the Court of the Member, MACT, XVI Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners have preferred this appeal.

entities.text: MACT, XVI Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 18.09.2018 at about 12.00 noon the deceased was riding a TVS XL Moped bearing registration No.KA-52-K-2275 and met with an accident near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk,
Thyamagondlu with a KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-42-F-1941, because of which the deceased expired.
The KSRTC bus is responsible to an extent of 75% for the accident and the deceased himself for the balance 25%.

The deceased was aged 78 Hemavathi vs Managing Director on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198021943/
2 years at the time of the accident.

sentences.text: The petitioners are grown up children of the deceased and were not dependant on him.
The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.79,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners who are legal representatives of the deceased have preferred this appeal.

4. In the course of the arguments, learned counsel for the appellants fairly submitted that he is not challenging the finding of the Tribunal insofar as it relates to as to who NC: 2023:KHC:29009 is responsible for the accident.
However, he contends that compensation has not been granted as per the law laid down by the Apex Court and the same requires to be enhanced.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent submits that the order of the Tribunal is in accordance with law and given the age of the deceased, notional income as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority cannot be considered as the same is determined taking into consideration an able bodied person and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. Admittedly, the deceased was aged 78 years at the time of the accident.

Given the present day medical advancement and increase in the life span of a person and given the fact that the deceased was fit enough to ride a moped, I deem it appropriate to fix his income notionally as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in consultation with Insurance NC:
2023:KHC:29009 Companie s, in the absence of any proof of income.
The same is taken at Rs.12,500/- per month.
7. Admittedly, the petitioners are children of the deceased who have attained majority and are not dependant upon the deceased.

In similar circumstances, the Apex Court in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. VINISH JAIN AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 3 SCC 619 has considered 50% of the income of the deceased towards loss of dependency to the legal heirs.

entities.text: NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. VINISH JAIN AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 3 SCC 619
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, in the present case, the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.12,500 (notional income)
/2x12x5 (multiplier)= Rs.3,75,000/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.
8.
The petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of estate and funeral expenses'.

9. The petitioners would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards 'loss of consortium'
and thus NC: 2023:KHC:29009 together are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- (40,000x4).
10. Further, the deceased is held to be responsible to an extent of 25% for causing the accident.
Thus, the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.4,23,750/- as compensation.
Thus, they are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,44,750/- (Rs.4,23,750 - Rs.79,000) over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Further, given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till realization.

Hence, the following:
